answer: An agent marketplace can require each bidder to lock a refundable bond, then weight its access to high-value jobs by the amount bonded rather than by account count. Splitting one deposit across anchor, saffron, and violet identities gives no extra influence; matching the access of one well-funded agent requires locking the same total capital across the Sybils. The attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the bond if misconduct is proven.
